content_blocks.text: View PDF
The Sustainable Procurement Duty , ou tlined in the Procurement Reform (Scotland) Act 2014 , requires you to think about how you can improve the:
Economic,
Social and
Environmental wellbeing
of the area(s) in which you operate – whether that is nationally or more locally. Particular focus should be on reducing inequality.

You can create a positive impact through every procurement exercise you undertake, regardless of its value or scope. This must be a key part of commodity/service profiling and strategy development rather than an optional area of interest. You must fully explore the possibilities with your User Intelligence Group and other stakeholders for your procurement.

heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: The Scottish Government has developed a number of tools to help you:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples

content_blocks.text: identify and work on how to increase economic, social and environmental benefits from your contract.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples

content_blocks.text: to agree your sustainable procurement priorities.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: You can use Sustainable Procurement tools when developing your commodity/service strategies. You will be required to register on this platform. These tools include:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: The Prioritisation Tool : an early stage tool that can be used at an organisation or category level
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: The Sustainability Test: : used at commodity/service level to identify potential scope of benefits
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: Life Cycle Impact Mapping : assesses economic, social and environmental impacts throughout the life cycle
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: The Flexible Framework Assessment Tool : self-assess current performance and actions required
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: By using these tools you can:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: identify what risks and opportunities can be targeted for each commodity
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: help manage those risks and exploit opportunities
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: include recommendations in your Commodity Strategy to be addressed as part of the procurement process
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools

content_blocks.text: As a matter of good practice, you should have completed the Sustainable Public Procurement Prioritisation Tool (to prioritise Sustainable Procurement aims) at a category or organisation level prior to working on your commodity/service strategy. If you are unsure, please speak to your manager to ask if this has been done.

content_blocks.text: in all procurement exercises.

content_blocks.text: To do so there are some specific actions you must take.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Develop transparent, detailed organisation Procurement Strategies and Annual Procurement Reports. This helps prospective tenderers identify opportunities ahead of the advertisement stage and plan resources. Procurement Strategies and Annual Procurement Reports are mandatory for Organisations who expect the value of their regulated contracts in that year to be £5 million or over (excluding VAT).
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Advertise regulated contracts and award notices through Public Contracts Scotland (PCS). PCS allows free and unlimited access to all potential bidders and smaller suppliers are more able to find opportunities.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Increase the use of debriefing. This supports the development and improvement of bidders, benefiting both the bidders and the organisation for future procurement exercises.

content_blocks.text: Your Organisation can “reserve” a competition so that only supported businesses can bid. In these cases, this must have been assessed as appropriate as there are specific rules around the reservation of competitions.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples

Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: The Guidance for Public Sector Buyers for the purchase of goods and services from Supported Businesses guidance document can be found at the bottom of this page. This document provides guidance for public sector buyers who procure goods and services, to enable them to better consider how procurement activity is conducted, and contracts are developed, in order to reduce barriers and enable participation of supported businesses in Public Sector Procurement
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities

content_blocks.text: A Supported Businesses DPS has been created to support the integration of disabled and disadvantaged citizens into the mainstream workforce

content_blocks.text: SME’s
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: The majority of businesses are SME’s. By doing everything you can to make it easy for SME’s to bid for your exercise then you are reaching the broader market and this will benefit your organisation as well as the broader economy.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Some things you can do to help SME’s access your process include:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: make sure your procurement exercise is advertised properly;
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: use lotting to enable smaller companies to identify potential opportunities;
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: make sure to include SME’s in pre-tender market engagement;
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: check that your tender and any pre-qualification are proportionate and will not exclude SME’s - e.g. do you really need such high levels of insurance for this process?
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: using a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) can offer benefits to SME’s in that, on qualifying they can access the contract at any time through its life and have access to smaller competitions within larger frameworks.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: There are many more things that you can do (or indeed not do) and you should take time to explore these as part of your strategy development. Speaking to colleagues, your UIG and contacting organisations such as the Federation of Small Businesses and the Supplier Development Programme can be very helpful.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Third Sector
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: The third sector, which includes charities, social enterprises and voluntary groups, delivers essential services, helps to improve people’s wellbeing and contributes to economic growth. It plays a vital role in supporting communities at a local level. The economic contribution of third sector organisations is steadily increasing and we expect this to continue in the coming years. Some things you should do to help Third Sector suppliers access your procurement include:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Identify and engage with any relevant Third Sector suppliers as early as possible in the process;
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Examine the market to identify any potential “blockers” to entry – e.g. are their providers for some of the requirement but not all? Would lotting help open up the opportunities ?
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Many of the actions that you can take to make sure SME’s are engaged can also support the inclusion of Third Sector organisations. Each council in Scotland has a "Third Sector Interface" (TSI) and further information can be obtained from these if you need help in identifying local Third Sector organisations.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Addressing Fair Work Practices
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: Fair Work practices are actions an employer adopts for the benefit of its workers. They are above the minimum legal requirements and reflect the five dimensions of the Fair Work Framework and the Scottish Government’s Fair Work First policy.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: When developing any procurement exercise, you must do so in line with Statutory Guidance . This requires you to consider how to address Fair Work practices in all procurement exercises before you start your procurement.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

content_blocks.text: To support this Fair Work First in Procurement guidance has been developed to offer additional guidance and practical tools for public bodies and suppliers. .
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Sustainable Procurement Duty Tools
Sustainable Procurement, Risks and Opportunities
Involving Supported Businesses, SMEs and Third Sector Suppliers

heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration

content_blocks.text: Sustainable procurement elements can also be included as part of your costing model and it’s important for you to review what models are available and assess where you think that sustainable elements can be considered.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration

heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: Information on Whole Life Costing and Life Cycle Costing can be found in Additional Resources
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: Lifecycle Impact Mapping
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: Focuses on social and environmental impact rather than cost. Life cycle impacts help the user identify and assess impacts. For example, it may help to focus attention on the disposal phase before the procurement is carried out. This allows you to build end-of-life management requirements into performance clauses for successful contractors and your own internal management procedures.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: Please note: Life cycle impact mapping can be used alongside life cycle costing as part of the procurement process.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: The Lifecycle impact Mapping t ool can be accessed by registering on the Sustainable Procurement Tools platform.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: When purchasing goods or services you can specify labels as a means of proof that you meet certain requirements.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: For example, does the product or service required have specific social, environmental, or other characteristics that would be verified by a label such as Fairtrade?
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing

content_blocks.text: Labels
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: There is specific guidance around the use of labels within procurement.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: To specify labels in your procurement exercise you need to meet the following criteria:
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: The labels can only concern criteria that are linked to the subject matter of the contract. These must be appropriate to define characteristics of the supplies or services;
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: They must be based on objective and non-discriminatory criteria
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: The label itself is established in an open and transparent procedure and accessible to all interested parties
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: The label requirements are set by a third party over which no potential bidder has any decisive influence
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: Rather than apply a label on a broad basis, if it’s more proportionate you can detail which label requirements are to be met. This will reduce the burden on bidders and could expand the number of capable bidders for your process.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels

content_blocks.text: Labels must comply with the label requirements of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 and equivalent labels must be accepted. Where the bidder can demonstrate it has not been possible to obtain either the label or an equivalent, through no fault of its own, you must accept other appropriate means of proof e.g. manufacturers technical dossiers.
heading_path: Economic, Social and Environmental Wellbeing Examples
Other Areas for Consideration
Whole Life and Life Cycle Costing
Labels
